summary.tldr: Lets senators and MPs choose the oath of allegiance, the oath of office, or both before taking their seat.
what_it_does: Renumbers section 128 of the Constitution Act, 1867 and lets every senator or MP take the oath of office instead of the oath of allegiance, or take both.
Adds a new oath of office to the Fifth Schedule, saying the person will carry out their duties in the best interest of Canada while upholding its Constitution.
Keeps the Constitution Acts, 1867 to 1982 reference in step with this change by treating it as including this bill.
who_it_affects: Members of the House of Commons
summary.background: The bill amends section 128 of the Constitution Act, 1867 and adds an oath of office to the Fifth Schedule.
